walkthroughs.body_html:
The cerebrum handles conscious thought.

The cerebellum coordinates muscles and balance. The medulla controls heart rate, breathing and blood pressure.

Damage from stroke or injury shows what areas do. CT scans give structure; PET scans show activity using a tracer.

Brain surgery is risky — damage to surrounding tissue can cause loss of function.

Spinal cord damage causes paralysis because motor signals cannot reach effectors.

Stem cell research aims to grow new nerve cells to bridge damage — promising but not routine.

mcqs.q: What is the key structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.
Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.

mcqs.q: What is the main role of mitochondria in a cell?
options: To carry out aerobic respiration, producing ATP that cells use as an energy currency.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Mitochondria produce energy by creating it from nothing.
Mitochondria store sunlight and release it for photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells (gametes).
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Mitosis and meiosis both produce gametes; they are basically the same.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
